articles.title: Woman wearing burka escorted out of Florida county meeting after playing call to prayer recording
articles.summary: A woman wearing a burka played an Islamic call to prayer recording at a Pinellas County commissioners meeting before a sheriff's deputy escorted her out.
articles.body: A woman wearing a burka was escorted out of a Florida county commissioners meeting on Tuesday after playing a recording of the Islamic call to prayer during the public comment period where residents spoke against the potential expansion of a local mosque amid concerns from some over its wording on zoning and agenda materials. The incident occurred as the Pinellas County Board of County Commissioners was listening to residents address the board. A woman covered head-to-toe in black, with only her left eye visible, and approached the podium. Rather than making a verbal statement, she activated a recording of the call to prayer. It was not immediately clear whether the gesture was a protest or a prank. PASTOR UNLEASHES ON DEARBORN AS RELIGIOUS TENSIONS ERUPT AT CITY COUNCIL MEETING: 'ENOUGH IS ENOUGH' The audio played for nearly a minute before Board Chairman Dave Eggers interrupted, pointing out that county rules require public speakers to deliver verbal comments rather than play recordings. "Ma’am, you’re going to have to stop … stop the music, stop the tape," Eggers said. TEXAS POLICE ADMIT OFFICER MADE INACCURATE FIRST AMENDMENT REMARKS AFTER PREACHER CITED AT PRIDE EVENT When the woman refused to comply, a Pinellas County Sheriff’s Office deputy approached the podium and escorted her out of the meeting room and the building. Her removal sparked immediate friction in the room, with several audience members shouting and arguing with Eggers over the decision. "Please. Just please exercise some decorum and kindness of your own," Eggers told the audience. "We’re all people living together here." He further clarified the board’s rules to the crowd. "We don’t allow taped things," he said. "You can record the meeting, but we don’t allow taped activity like that. We ask you to come here and make comments, and that was not a comment. That’s why she was asked to step out." The incident came during a public period where multiple residents decried an Oct. 13 vote in which the board voted 4-3 to approve a land-use amendment for the expansion of the Masjid Al Rahman mosque, which was referred to in presentations and documents as a "community assembly facility." LAWSUIT ACCUSES DEARBORN, MICHIGAN, OF BEING 'HOSTILE TO CHRISTIANS AND JEWS' WITH ISLAMIC DISPLAYS The vote changed the property's land use from residential rural to public and semi-public, which would allow the facility's owner to replace the building with a newer structure 1,000 feet larger. During Tuesday's meeting, public speakers spoke out against the facility, some citing the treatment of women in Muslim-majority countries. "It is about the big picture and the long term," one woman told the commission. "By allowing this mosque to expand in our area, you are participating in the expansion of a totalitarian ideology which is fundamentally opposed to Western American values. Expansion of the ideology of Islam is not good for women's rights." Another woman supported the mosque: "They want to turn it to face Mecca, and they want it to look a little more like a mosque instead of a house," she said. "We have no problems with them. We've been their neighbors for many years." Commissioner Vince Nowicki reportedly questioned why the mosque wasn't described in plain language in government documents. "Residents read these materials to understand what is being proposed near them, and they should get the same plain description in every case, no matter the applicant," Nowicki wrote in an email to County Administrator Barry Burton, Florida Politics reported. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Pinellas County Sheriff’s Office confirmed that the woman was escorted from the premises without further incident and will not face any criminal charges.

articles.title: Do water leak detectors actually work? Here’s what home experts say
articles.summary: I reached out to home experts to learn more about water leak detectors and exactly how they work. Here’s how you can use them to avoid frozen pipes.
articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like whether bath sheets are actually different from towels. It’s expected that homeowners have things like smoke and carbon monoxide detectors in their homes to keep them and their families safe. But another type of home-related detector that’s also worth considering is a water leak detector. Depending on where you live and what type of home you have, a water leak detector can be a very beneficial tool, since it can help track water pressure and temperature, and help you get ahead of frozen pipes in the winter, which can be a major inconvenience — and a costly one if the pipes burst. To learn more about how water leak detectors actually work and how to shop for one, I spoke to Lou Manfredini, a seasoned home expert at Ace Hardware*, who says that there are several different types of detectors to consider. *Any inclusion of products sold at Ace Hardware in this story was made independently of Manfredini, who we only consulted for guidance. We did not ask Manfredini for product recommendations. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Highly-rated water leak detectors and sensors All of the products below have at least a four-star rating from 500 or more shoppers on Amazon (or 100 or more at another retailer if it’s unavailable at Amazon). This water leak detector from GoveeLife includes a set of three water leak sensors that can detect when water starts pooling around it, such as under the pipe of a sink, for example. It also includes a WiFi adapter, since it’s a smart device that connects to the brand’s app on your phone, where it can alert you of a leak — it will also send you an email notification and/or a text message. You’ll also get a set of six AAA batteries. The WiFi hub and the water leak sensors also operate within 1,800 feet of each other, so you can use them in very large homes or buildings. This water leak detector works with Amazon Alexa to send you notifications if it senses water or flooding on the ground, so if you’re away during a storm, for example, it can let you know water has entered your basement, bathroom or living room. It comes with an adapter and a power cable with a sensor connected to it. It detects water drops as well as if it’s been submerged in water, according to the brand. It’s one of the most affordable options on this list and a great one to try if you’re new water leak detectors and have a small budget. This water leak detector connects directly to the pipes of your home’s water supply. It fits pipes of different diameters and materials, including brass, copper and PVC. Additionally, this water leak detector doesn’t require installation by a professional and only takes about five minutes to connect, according to the brand. The device can also alert you when there’s a change in water flow inside the pipes, not just a leak going outward. This water leak detector from Moen monitors both water floor and temperature in the water going through the pipes in your home’s water supply. Similar to the Hydrific detector, it attaches to the pipe and can send an alert straight to your phone via Moen’s Smart Water Network app. It also detects temperature changes in water (not just flow), so it can help prevent your pipes from freezing by turning off the water if the temperature drops below a certain degree. While you can technically install it yourself, the brand recommends having a professional do it. How do water leak detectors work? Water leak detectors, also sometimes called water leak sensors (which are technically a different type of detector), are systems that monitor water activity in your home. “There are several types, but basically they sense when water is present and will sound an alarm or send you a notification to your phone or computer to alert you of a leak,” says Manfredini. “The basic leak detectors are placed in areas where there may be a concern for water leaking.” This includes areas like under a sink, under a water heater or in a basement, according to Manfredini. He further explains that they essentially watch for what seems like an excessive use of water, which can sometimes be caused by a burst pipe or a running toilet. If it’s a point-of-use detector, it can literally sense when water is dripping on it or if it’s pooling around the device on the floor or the surface of a cabinet under a faucet for example. An in-line water detector connects to your pipes to determine changes in flow and temperature (more on this below). What are the different types of water leak detectors? There are a few different types of water leak detectors, but in general, you’ll find that many come in one of two forms, according to Chris Petri, owner of Petri Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Drain Cleaning. These are the types you typically see: Point-of-use water leak detectors: These types of water leak detectors literally sense water that is flooding around them. They’re commonly placed under a sink or water heater, according to Manfredini, and they will sound an alarm if they come in contact with water droplets or water pooling around them. Brands like Moen and GoveeLife have point-of-use water leak detectors. These types of detectors are usually circular or oblong in shape and adhere to a flat surface under a water source. Some water leak sensors include a power cable you place on the floor that will detect if water has already started to pool around it or if it’s submerged in water. You can use these types of sensors residentially or commercially, according to Manfredini. In-line water leak detectors: “These are installed directly into your water main and use an internal turbine to measure water flow,” says Petri. “The device learns your home’s normal usage patterns—such as flow rate, duration, and volume.” If it detects a change in flow of your water (some also detect change in temperature), it will send you an alert and can automatically shut off the flow of water to prevent any flooding or freezing of pipes. This is also how a water leak detector can help prevent pipes from freezing, since some of them also monitor temperature. What’s also great about these types of detectors is that you don’t actually have to wait for it to start flooding or for it to touch water for it to alert you, according to Petri. The Moen Flo Smart Water Leak Detection Alarm is an example of this type. What should you consider before buying a water leak detector? “Every home benefits from proactive leak detection,” says Petri. “Waiting until a leak is visually noticeable often means damage has already occurred, especially since leaks frequently happen in hidden areas or while you are away.” Getting a water leak detector that works for your type of space is important in determining if it’s a worthy investment, so it needs to have certain features. “Key features to consider include automatic water shutoff capabilities, smart notifications (such as app alerts), placement requirements, and whether you need whole-home coverage (in-line) or targeted area protection (point-of-use).” Meet our home experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. We did not ask Manfredini for product recommendations. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home and kitchen appliances, including travel-friendly carbon monoxide detectors, leaf blowers, candle warmers and more. For this story, I talked to two home appliance and plumbing experts for their guidance on water leak detectors. articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil’s ‘true president’, vows to lead opposition from US
articles.summary: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro has declared himself the country’s “true president-elect”, alleged electoral fraud in President Luiz Inácio Lula da
articles.body: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro has declared himself the country’s “true president-elect”, alleged electoral fraud in President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election and vowed to lead Brazil’s opposition from the United States, where he has arrived with his family after leaving the country.In a lengthy statement addressed to Brazilians and the international community on Wednesday, Flávio rejected the description of his departure as a flight from Brazil, saying he had left to escape what he described as political persecution and an increasingly authoritarian political system. He also thanked US president Donald Trump and Argentine president Javier Milei for their support, portraying the United States as a place where his family could find the legal security he claimed was no longer available at home.“I want to make this clear: I did not flee Brazil; I left for Brazil’s sake” – he wrote, arguing that remaining in the country would have prevented him from exercising political leadership.Flávio alleged that the October 25 presidential election was marred by fraud, claiming that Lula gained more than 10 million votes between the first and second rounds in what he called a “mathematical impossibility”. He also challenged a decision to extend voting hours in some locations, accused judicial authorities of acting beyond their jurisdiction and argued that alleged campaign violations justified annulling the Lula-Alckmin ticket.The statement, however, did not provide evidence establishing that electoral fraud had occurred. Brazil’s Liberal Party (PL), which backed Flávio’s candidacy, had earlier recognised the official election result while calling for the issues raised by the campaign to be addressed through political and democratic debate.Flávio also accused the Supreme Federal Court of orchestrating a campaign of political persecution against him and his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. He claimed that judicial action against him could progress from passport seizure to electronic monitoring, censorship, house arrest and eventual political conviction. He insisted that no arrest warrant had been issued against him and denied committing any crime.The senator said he had brought his family to the US to protect them and would continue his political activities from abroad. Drawing comparisons with figures including French wartime leader Charles de Gaulle and Venezuelan opposition leaders, he portrayed his departure as a continuation of a struggle for democracy rather than an abandonment of Brazilian politics.Addressing lawmakers and governors allied with him, Flávio said he would lead the opposition from the US, promising to speak on behalf of supporters who, he claimed, could not freely express themselves in Brazil. He named senator Rogério Marinho as his candidate for the presidency of the Senate and said he would soon outline a strategy to mobilise the opposition through what he described as peaceful and legitimate means.The statement marks a further escalation in Flávio’s challenge to Lula’s victory. He had previously said he would seek the annulment of the election, while the PL subsequently acknowledged the result proclaimed by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court.You use AI every day. articles.title: Death of US actress Hayden Panettiere ruled accidental, ending local police probe
articles.summary: The Heroes and Nashville star died in August from the toxic effects of fentanyl, Xanax and several other drugs.
articles.body:
The death of US actress Hayden Panettiere has been ruled accidental, ending a local probe into her death, police in South Carolina have said.

The Heroes and Nashville star died in August from the toxic effects of fentanyl, Xanax and several other drugs in her system, at the age of 36.

Citing the medical examiner's report last month that found Panettiere died from a drug overdose, the Greenville Police Department said it had "concluded its investigation" into her death.

The US Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) reportedly joined a local police probe. It is unclear if that investigation has also concluded. The BBC has contacted the DEA for comment.

"Based on the Medical Examiner's determination and the findings of the investigation, Hayden Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental," police said in a statement.

Authorities, including the DEA, were reportedly investigating the circumstances of Panettiere's death, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS News.

A spokesperson for Greenville Police Department could not comment on what the DEA was investigating when contacted by the BBC.

Panettiere, who had spoken openly about her struggles with substance abuse , was found unresponsive in a South Carolina residence on 16 August.

Last month, the Greenville County Coroner's Office confirmed the former child star had died from an accidental drug overdose that included fentanyl - a synthetic opioid that has killed hundreds of thousands of Americans over the past five years alone.

The coroner also found methocarbamol - a prescription muscle relaxant - and quetiapine - an anti-psychotic medication used to treat certain mental health conditions.

The coroner's office had said crews treated a woman in "cardiac arrest" and her autopsy showed "no signs of trauma" contributing to her death.

Panettiere's ex-boyfriend, Brian Hickerson - who has admitted to abusing her - and his brother Zack were with her when emergency services arrived, according to a police report from the day she died.

articles.title: A Maui family bought an oceanfront home for $8.05 million in 2014 and gutted it to the studs in 2020; after initially asking $24.85 million, the renovated estate sold for $18.5 million in October 2026
articles.summary: A renovated oceanfront estate in Maui’s exclusive Makena neighbourhood has sold for $18.5 million, making it the Hawaiian island’s most expensive
articles.body: A renovated oceanfront estate in Maui’s exclusive Makena neighbourhood has sold for $18.5 million, making it the Hawaiian island’s most expensive on-market residential sale of 2026 so far. The four-bedroom property, which sits on more than an acre of coastal land, attracted a buyer despite a slowdown in Hawaii’s ultra-luxury housing market, according to reporting by The Wall Street Journal, Mansion Global and Robb Report. Originally purchased by a family for $8.05 million in 2014, the home underwent a comprehensive renovation six years later. Its eventual sale price was substantially below the $24.85 million asking price at which it entered the market in 2024, reflecting the gap between sellers’ expectations and buyers’ growing selectivity in the high-end property sector.A complete transformation of the oceanfront homeBuilt in 1991, the 4,500-square-foot residence was extensively outdated when the owners decided to renovate it. In 2020, the family stripped the interiors back to the structural framework, creating an opportunity to redesign the home around its coastal setting. The renovation was led by the owner and her mother, working alongside KLC Design & Build, a woman-led contracting firm. The project focused on natural materials, locally inspired craftsmanship and a layout that connects indoor living spaces with the surrounding landscape.Shell Reef limestone, featuring fossilised marine material, became a defining element of the redesign. The pale stone extends through much of the interior and around the swimming pool, while a retractable glass wall opens the living areas towards the outdoors. The finished home blends understated luxury with a relaxed island aesthetic. Local avocado wood and seaglass feature in the breakfast bar, while lava rock lines the outdoor showers. A custom living-room light installation incorporates a surfboard alongside woven pendant elements, adding a distinctly Hawaiian touch to the interiors. The property was sold furnished, excluding selected artwork, allowing the new owner to move into a fully designed residence without undertaking another major furnishing project.A private coastal setting adds to its appealThe property’s location in Makena was another major selling point. Set on a natural promontory along Maui’s South Shore, the estate overlooks the Pacific and offers direct access to a small coastal cove. Big Beach, one of the area’s best-known stretches of shoreline, is also nearby. The outdoor amenities include a swimming pool, two hot tubs, a home gym and a putting green. The combination of privacy, ocean access and indoor-outdoor living distinguishes the property from homes that rely primarily on elaborate interiors or formal entertaining spaces. Makena is known for its high-value residential properties and discreet luxury market. The neighbourhood also borders an expansive private residential development operated by Discovery Land Company, adding to its appeal among buyers seeking seclusion.Sale comes amid a more selective luxury marketThe $18.5 million transaction stands out against a cooling market for Hawaii homes priced above $10 million. According to Mansion Global, sales in that segment had fallen by 50% compared with the corresponding period a year earlier. The final price was $6.35 million below the property’s original $24.85 million asking price, a reduction of approximately 25.6%. Even so, the sale highlights the continued appeal of distinctive coastal estates when their location, design and condition meet the expectations of a selective buyer pool.Public property records and real estate listings identify the transaction as the sale of the residence at 7421 Makena Road, which closed on October 21, 2026, for $18.5 million. The property measures approximately 4,544 square feet and occupies a parcel of just over an acre. While the sale does not reverse the broader slowdown in Hawaii’s ultra-luxury market, it demonstrates that exceptional coastal properties can still command multimillion-dollar prices, even when sellers must adjust their initial expectations.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Actor Mandy Patinkin urges Jewish voters to support Abdul El-Sayed for their own 'safety'
articles.summary: Jewish Actor Mandy Patinkin urged Jewish voters to back Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Senate race in several social media videos.
articles.body: Actor Mandy Patinkin has posted several videos on social media, including one on Friday, urging Jewish voters to support Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed if they're concerned about their "safety" in the country. "Jewish safety depends on a real multiracial democracy, and Abdul is the one fighting to protect it," the "Homeland" and "The Princess Bride" actor said in one such video. Patinkin, who is also Jewish, said that El-Sayed's Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, was pushing a political movement attacking the "rights and dignity of certain people" and argued that El-Sayed was the only candidate fighting for democracy. "Jewish safety is tied to the health of our democracy," Patinkin said. "We can’t protect one without protecting the other. And in this Senate race, Abdul is the candidate who understands that and is willing to fight for it." ABDUL EL-SAYED HITS BACK AT ISRAEL QUESTIONS, SUGGESTS HIS NAME AND FAITH ARE BEHIND PRESS SCRUTINY Patinkin continued to voice his support for El-Sayed in another video posted on Sunday, in which he called out efforts to make people "afraid" of the Democratic candidate because of his name and Muslim background, suggesting the criticism was similar to how Jewish people have been treated because of their identity. "It’s hard for me to hear Muslims and Arabs talked about this way without thinking about our own Jewish history," Patinkin said. "We know what it’s like to have people treat your identity as a reason to distrust you, to make you seem threatening just because of who you are. I’m not telling anyone what they have to believe about Abdul. I’m asking people to recognize that this kind of talk should sound familiar to Jews." "Who is going to protect the democracy that has helped keep Jews safe in America? Abdul," he added. "Who is going to stand up for the rights of all of us? Abdul. Because I believe protecting our community means protecting the democracy we all depend on. Please vote for Abdul El-Sayed and get him in the Senate seat." Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed and Rogers campaigns for comment but did not immediately receive a response. ABDUL EL-SAYED INVOKES JFK TO DISMISS 'CRAZY' QUESTIONS OVER FAMILY'S ALLEGED TIES TO MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD Rabbi Yaakov Menken, managing director of the Coalition for Jewish Values, criticized Patinkin's "lack of actual knowledge" about whether El-Sayed would support Jewish safety. "Few candidates have expressed disdain for Jewish safety more than Abdul El-Sayed, who attempted to explain away a terror attack on Jewish preschoolers due to a war on terror 6,000 miles away, and who called the rescue of Jewish hostages from torture, rape, and murder, ‘genocide,’" Menken told Fox News Digital. El-Sayed caused controversy in March when he responded to an attack on a Michigan synagogue by saying "Hurt people, hurt people." Federal investigators say a gunman inspired and radicalized by Hezbollah crashed into the place of worship seeking to kill as many Jewish people as he could. The alleged attacker was a Lebanese-born man who a week earlier had lost relatives in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon. El-Sayed later apologized for his comments about the attack. Menken said the Democratic candidate "refused to endorse the right of Jews to their own identity, opinions, and self-governance, and campaigned alongside Hasan Piker until other Democrats prevailed upon him to stop. And, of course, when confronted about family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood and its genocidal antisemitism, El-Sayed has called it an attack on his religion." "To call Patinkin deluded and naive would be the height of understatement," the rabbi added. "El-Sayed's values are not those that made America a great and welcoming country." JEWISH MICHIGAN DEMOCRATS ADMIT THEY WILL VOTE REPUBLICAN IF ABDUL EL-SAYED BECOMES NOMINEE Patinkin previously supported New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's 2025 campaign, celebrating the first night of Hanukkah with the democratic socialist after he was elected. Throughout his campaign and since taking office, Mamdani has faced accusations of antisemitism. articles.title: Prince William inherited the $1.3 billion Duchy of Cornwall, spanning 128,000 acres, after Queen Elizabeth II’s death; earning $31 million annually from it, he now plans to sell 20% to fund housing and green projects
articles.summary: Prince William is using one of the British royal family's most valuable assets to pursue causes close to his heart, with plans to sell a portion of his
articles.body: Prince William is using one of the British royal family's most valuable assets to pursue causes close to his heart, with plans to sell a portion of his vast estate to fund housing, environmental recovery and renewable energy projects.The Prince of Wales, 44, took control of the Duchy of Cornwall after the death of his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, in September 2022. The estate, which spans more than 128,000 acres, is valued at over $1.3 billion and provides William with an annual private income of nearly $31 million.However, the future king is looking beyond the traditional role of the estate as a source of income. According to a report by The Times, William plans to sell around 20% of the Duchy's assets, potentially raising an estimated $670 million to support a new approach centred on social needs, nature recovery and clean energy.Why Prince William wants to reshape the Duchy of CornwallEstablished in 1337, the Duchy of Cornwall was created to provide an income for the heir to the British throne and support the household and public responsibilities associated with the role. It has traditionally consisted of land, property and other assets managed on behalf of the heir apparent.William inherited control of the estate when his father, King Charles III, became monarch following Queen Elizabeth II's death. When William eventually becomes king, control will pass to his eldest son, Prince George, continuing the centuries-old tradition.Under William's leadership, however, the estate is being encouraged to take a more active role in addressing local challenges. The reported plan to sell a fifth of its assets would allow it to focus its resources on five key areas, including Cornwall, Dartmoor, the Isles of Scilly, Bath and parts of London.Duchy chief executive Will Bax has outlined a vision in which the organisation evaluates its presence according to the positive impact it can deliver."If we don’t see an opportunity for positive impact, then perhaps we don’t need to be a part of that place," Bax told The Times."But where there is social need and where there is environmental challenge and where there is an opportunity to enable change, then we’ll be a great partner in working with people to achieve that."The approach reflects William's broader interest in using his position and resources to address social and environmental concerns.Tackling homelessness through housing projectsOne of William's priorities for the Duchy is addressing homelessness, an issue he has also made central to his wider Homewards initiative.The project seeks to develop practical, locally driven solutions to homelessness, bringing together organisations and communities to explore ways of preventing people from losing their homes.In 2024, Ben Murphy, estate director at the Duchy of Cornwall, explained that William had asked the estate to address homelessness in Cornwall and other areas where it operates."As one of his key priorities for the Duchy of Cornwall, Prince William asked us to address the homelessness challenge within Cornwall and other areas where the estate resides," Murphy said.The Duchy is already developing social housing in Nansledan, near Newquay in Cornwall. The project is part of a broader effort to create communities that combine housing with local services and commercial spaces.Another planned development on Market Street in Newquay aims to create a new high street featuring independent businesses, local artisans and community enterprises. The project is expected to be completed in 2028 and is intended to help strengthen the local economy.These developments illustrate how the estate's property portfolio could be used to support communities beyond its traditional financial role.Why William is redirecting money from Dartmoor PrisonThe Prince of Wales has also taken steps to redirect income from an estate asset that is no longer being used for its original purpose.Dartmoor Prison, which has remained empty since July 2024, had generated approximately $2 million a year in rental income for William. Rather than continue to retain that money, he directed that the annual amount be returned to the local community through the Princetown Community Fund.According to a September press release, the fund will support projects delivering lasting social, economic and environmental benefits for people in Princetown and the surrounding Dartmoor area.The decision aligns with the wider direction of the Duchy under William: ensuring that assets and income are connected to the needs of the communities in which the estate operates.Princess Kate's early childhood initiative finds a partner in the DuchyWilliam's plans also intersect with the work of his wife, Princess Kate, particularly her focus on early childhood development and the role of nature in children's well-being.Kate's Centre for Early Childhood has partnered with the Duchy of Cornwall to explore how time spent outdoors can support the mental well-being and development of young children, as well as the people who care for them.The collaboration, launched in Nansledan, examines how nature, creativity and relationships can help children develop the social and emotional skills that contribute to lifelong health and well-being."This project is about exploring how nature, creativity and relationships can best support the healthy development of babies and young children," Kate said in a video."We believe that taking a whole-child approach is important, and nature becomes a wonderful place to explore how we can successfully nurture the social and emotional skills that underpin lifelong health and wellbeing."The initiative connects the Duchy's environmental ambitions with Kate's long-standing interest in the early years of childhood, highlighting how the estate's land can be used for projects that benefit families and local communities.Cornwall remains important to William and his familyBeyond its financial value and public-facing projects, the Duchy is also connected to William and Kate's family life.Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly are among the places where the family regularly spends time. The Prince and Princess of Wales have also released photographs and videos of their children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, taken in Cornwall as part of birthday celebrations this year.You use AI every day. articles.title: New 123.4-proof whiskey prompts expert warning that stronger isn't always better
articles.summary: Bottled at 123.4 proof from estate-grown grains, Frey Ranch's barrel strength whiskey pushes the upper limits of what oak aging can deliver.
articles.body: A new whiskey from a family-owned Nevada distillery is bottled at 123.4 proof, a number that might intimidate some whiskey drinkers. But does a higher proof necessarily mean a better drink? The answer isn't as simple as the number on the bottle, according to a spirits expert and the distillery's owners. MAKING WHISKEY AT HOME COULD LAND YOU IN PRISON, BUT SUPREME COURT MAY CHANGE THAT Aged in oak barrels for five to eight years, the Third Harvest whiskey from Frey Ranch Farmers & Distillers in Fallon, Nevada, is 61.7% alcohol by volume (ABV), the equivalent of 123.4 proof. Colby and Ashley Frey, co-founders and owners of the distillery, spoke with Fox News Digital about their farming heritage and the new whiskey. Colby Frey's family began farming in northern Nevada in 1854, and he's kept the legacy alive. "We've been continually farming in Nevada ever since," he told Fox News Digital. The Third Harvest whiskey is made from a blend of corn, rye, malted barley, wheat and triticale, a wheat-rye hybrid. HIGH-ALCOHOL, READY-TO-DRINK COCKTAILS SPARK OVERCONSUMPTION CONCERNS FOR GEN Z DRINKERS Frey Ranch grows 100% of its grains on-site, and the sole purpose of those grains is to become whiskey. "It's really rare in the whiskey world to do that," Colby said. Despite its high proof, the number is not outrageous, Derek Brown of Drink Company, a Washington, D.C.-based hospitality consulting and events company, told Fox News Digital. "There are many whiskies that are barrel strength, although this one is certainly toward the upper limit," Brown said, adding that some of his favorite bottles are high proof. Brown noted that, ideally, a high-proof spirit will have more complex flavors from the barrels it's aged in as opposed to an overpowering alcohol flavor. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "It can definitely produce a burning sensation and be too much if the other flavors, especially those from wood maturation, are not also present," he said. The Freys acknowledged that this specific bottle has a high proof, but they said the number doesn't tell the whole story. "We like to pick our whiskey and proof our whiskey based on flavor profiles, not on proof," Ashley Frey said. "So, we'll always taste it at various proofs, and, for us, we want to be able to say we're tasting the best expression of our grain as a whiskey." This batch, she added, "is going to be for somebody who's really searching and has a refined palate that's able to pull out all these flavor profiles." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Brown agreed, saying it's "definitely for the initiated." "However, if you're willing to take a chance, it's entirely reasonable to add water or an ice cube to whiskey if it's too strong for you," he said. Those who are sensitive to bitter, bold flavors might be better off choosing a different beverage, Brown recommended. "It's really a piece of me and Colby's hard work and heritage and love for the land and agriculture that's expressed through a bottle of whiskey," Ashley Frey said. articles.title: King Charles shows off dance moves on second day of Caribbean tour
articles.summary: Earlier in the day, the King paid his respects to the island's fallen servicemen and women.
articles.body:
The King shook off royal formality and replaced it with some dance moves on the second day of his nine-day visit to the Caribbean.

Armed with a pair of maracas in the colours of the flag of the Bahamas, Charles joined a Junkanoo - a cultural event and carnival designed to celebrate island life.

Amidst the feathered headdresses and brightly coloured costumes in the afternoon Caribbean heat, the King, dressed in a suit and sunglasses, joined dancers at the front of parade to cheers from the crowd.

It was a lighter mood coming after the King's arrival on Tuesday where he delivered a speech acknowledging the pain of the slave trade, describing "the suffering of the past".

King acknowledges 'suffering of the past' as Caribbean tour begins

Speaking at an event in the Bahamas celebrating local youth on Tuesday, the King said the country's culture was "born out of darkness", and it was "only right" to acknowledge historic injustices.

Charles began the second day of his trip by paying his respects to fallen members of the Royal Bahamas Defence Force (RBDF).

The King, wearing a set of medals and sunglasses, spoke with servicemen and women before he laid a wreath at the Flamingo Monument, which commemorates four RBDF Marines killed when Cuban MiG fighter aircraft sunk HMBS Flamingo in May 1980.

Later, on a visit to the Bahamas Boxing Academy, the King found young fighters and the head coach wearing an image of himself emblazoned on club t-shirts showing the King complete with a crown, gloves and a boxing belt.

"He loved it, he loved it," said Jermaine Gibson, president of a neighbouring boxing club who wore one of the t-shirts. "He said it was really good and we gave him one of his own."

The King watched two young fighters sparring in the ring at the academy which trains boys and girls from the age of eight to 18 years old.

"I might see you at a Commonwealth Games," the King told a group of children at the boxing academy.

Protecting this region from climate change is a theme of the King's trip and was the focus of his visit to the Bonefish Pond National Park. The site was once a rubbish dump but has been redeveloped and now protects 1,235 acres of mangroves.

The King walked along a new boardwalk through the wetlands to see the conservation work being done to protect this vulnerable, low lying island from climate change.

He met students carrying out field work in the wetland waters asking them about their exams and ambitions to be marine biologists.

"We've so been looking forward to this," said Joanne Smith, President of the Bahamas National Trust Council.

"We want more Bahamians to get involved in our national parks so they can use it to better themselves… we are so pleased to have the King here, this is really significant for us."

Then it was on to the Junkanoo, where the King could be seen dancing alongside attendees dressed in feathered headdresses and bright costumes.

The history of the Junkanoo is not clear but it's believed it emerged out of the slave trade when enslaved men and women were given time off to mark Christmas.

A small protest near the parade was moved on by the police.

The King ended his day with a garden reception at Government House in Nassau where he met Bahamians who have made significant contributions to public life.

In a speech, Dame Cynthia A Pratt, the governor general of the Bahamas who is the King's representative on the island, described her pride at Charles visiting the country for the first time since 1973.

"We trust that your time in our capital will reflect the legendary hospitality of our people," said Dame Cynthia.

"We pray that this royal visit further strengthens the enduring bonds of friendship between the Crown and the Bahamian people."

On Thursday, the Caribbean tour leaves the Bahamas as the King continues his visit in Guyana.

The trip has been planned alongside the governments of the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda with an emphasis on honouring the past but also looking forward to the ambition and possibility for future generations.

The King will move to Guyana later this week where his engagements will focus on the environment and biodiversity.

He will then visit Antigua and Barbuda, where he will be joined by Queen Camilla, for the CHOGM and his keynote speech as leader of the Commonwealth.

The biennial summit will bring together leaders of 56 Commonwealth countries to address shared challenges and advance cooperation.

articles.title: In SC, biological women oppose equal rights for transgender women
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Striking a discordant note among a clutch of petitions challenging the Transgender Amendment Act for denying right to gender
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Striking a discordant note among a clutch of petitions challenging the Transgender Amendment Act for denying right to gender self-determination, an all-women NGO Wednesday appealed to the Supreme Court not to confer trans-women, biological males identifying as females, the spectrum of constitutional rights guaranteed to biological women.‘Women’s Declaration International India’ through senior advocate Amit Sibal told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that “self-professed or socio-cultural gender identity or certificate or document cannot change a person’s biological sex or enable a biological male to access the entire spectrum of rights, protections and entitlements created specifically for biological females.” Differentiating between sex and gender, the petitioner said, “Sex and gender identity are distinct; gender identity concerns a person’s deeply felt internal experience, while sex is the stable immutable biological category on which numerous constitutional and statutory protections for women are premised.”SC asked Centre to respond to the petition with a comprehensive affidavit that also dealt with the other petitions challenging the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026. SG Tushar Mehta said a comprehensive affidavit is being drafted but gave an indication of what would be govt’s stand in defence of the erasure of gender self-determination clause, which was replaced by medically determined gender.He asked: “Can a transwoman be permitted to compete in a sporting event for women? Should a policewoman conduct physical search of a person with male genitals but perceives himself to be a woman? If a biologically male criminal perceives himself to be a woman, should police be barred from arresting him after sunset?”Drawing the court’s attention to a recent incident in the US relating to a transgender inmate, who perceives himself to be a woman but impregnated two women inmates, Mehta said several aspects needed to be kept in mind while adjudicating the petitions.A male becoming a trans-woman will violate affirmative measures for women under the Constitution, equal opportunity to women in employment, women’s bodily privacy and personal security in sex-segregated spaces and criminal law safeguards, the petitioner said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: NDA wins 1 6 of 28 seats, Congress falters in MLC polls
articles.summary: BJP-led NDA won 16 of 28 seats in MLC polls held across four states, sweeping all four Karnataka legislative council constituencies, dealing a setback to
articles.body: BJP-led NDA won 16 of 28 seats in MLC polls held across four states, sweeping all four Karnataka legislative council constituencies, dealing a setback to Congress. Bihar and Maharashtra delivered split verdicts, while BJP led in UP as counting of paper ballots continued from Tuesday till late Wednesday.In Karnataka, JD(S) wrested Bengaluru teachers from Congress, while BJP won North East teachers, West graduates and South East graduates. D K Shivakumar, facing his first polls as CM, said Congress would take corrective measures. “We respect the verdict. We had expected two seats, but that did not happen,” he said.Congress had demanded a return to ballot papers.PK’s party gets 1st council seat, ends CPI’s lone representationBut results suggested its setbacks stemmed from organisational weaknesses. Party insiders said 19 ministers assigned to oversee 133 assembly segments failed to deliver, amid growing internal differences. BJP and JD(S) coordinated more closely than in previous polls.In Bihar, NDA won four of eight seats, while RJD and Prashant Kishor’s Jan Suraaj won one each. Independents took the remaining two. All four sitting teachers’ constituency MLCs lost, while incumbents retained all four graduates’ seats. RJD-backed Sanjeev Kumar defeated BJP veteran Nawal Yadav, a five-term MLC who had held Patna teachers for three decades. Jan Suraaj’s Suresh Prasad Rai defeated former Bihar Congress chief Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in Darbhanga teachers, giving Kishor’s party its first council seat and ending CPI’s lone representation.In UP, BJP won six seats and SP three among nine seats declared by Wednesday evening. Counting continued in Lucknow and Varanasi graduates’ constituencies. Independent Dhruv Tripathi, who later joined BJP, won Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers for a fourth consecutive term, defeating Independent Rajiv Yadav by 307 votes.Maharashtra’s five MLC seats were closely contested between Mahayuti and opposition alliance MVA, with both winning two each. Among Mahayuti’s victories, BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade won Pune teachers, while Sena’s Kiran Sarnaik took Amravati teachers. Sharad Pawar’s NCP-SP won two.In Nagpur, outcome remained uncertain after over 40 hours of counting, with BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale and Congress’s Abhijeet Wanjari trading leads through the day.State Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal said: “Our party contested three seats and made every effort to win. A large number of votes were declared invalid, which is a matter of concern.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
